Index: Panel A. IRRs are per 10-percentile increase in the index. Unless noted, models are negative binomial (NB2) with the dispersion (alpha) estimated by maximum likelihood and an offset of log(adults aged ≥45 years). The primary analysis is the SVI and EDI model adjusted for metropolitan status. Second term: metropolitan status (RUCC 1-3 vs 4-9), ordinal RUCC per 1-code increase, or log population density per 1-unit increase.

The offset makes each model a model for the facility rate but weights every county equally; primary estimates therefore describe the average county. Population-weighted models weight counties by adults aged ≥45 years (normalized to mean 1) and estimate the association for the average adult; robust (HC0) standard errors. Under these weights the Kish effective sample size is 314 of 3,144 counties, and the largest 1% of counties carry 22.3% of the weight.

Stratified rows marked Poisson: in these strata every county had zero or one facility, the NB2 dispersion estimate lay on its boundary (alpha = 0) and the information matrix could not be inverted at the optimizer's stopping point; the maximum-likelihood NB2 fit at alpha = 0 is the Poisson fit, shown here (see Supplementary Table S4). Facility totals differ by index because counties without an index value are excluded.
Panel B compares specifications for the unadjusted and metropolitan-adjusted models.

CCT = cardiac computed tomography; CI = confidence interval; CMR = cardiac magnetic resonance; EDI = economic deprivation index; IRR = incidence rate ratio; NB2 = negative binomial (quadratic variance); NE = not estimable; RUCC = Rural-Urban Continuum Code; SDI = Social Deprivation Index; SVI = Social Vulnerability Index.
